summary: This ROS wiki page explains that ROS software is organized into packages, which may contain nodes, libraries, datasets, configuration files, or third-party software. It describes the common package directory structure, the command-line tools used to manage packages, and the Python and C++ client library APIs for querying package information. The page is for ROS 1, with ROS 2 users directed to separate documentation.
one_line: ROS wiki page describing ROS packages: their file structure, command-line tools, and Python and C++ APIs for querying package information.
key_facts: In ROS, a package is the smallest individual thing you can build and the unit of release, with one debian package for each ROS package.
A ROS package is simply a directory descended from ROS_PACKAGE_PATH that has a package.xml file in it.
Packages are easy to create by hand or with tools like catkin_create_pkg.
ROS packages generally follow a 'Goldilocks' principle: enough functionality to be useful, but not so much that the package is heavyweight and difficult to use.
The include/package_name directory holds C++ include headers, which should be exported in the CMakeLists.txt.
The msg/ and srv/ folders contain Message (msg) and Service (srv) types respectively.
The CHANGELOG.rst file can be automatically injected into binary packaging and into the wiki page for the package.
The rospack tool finds and retrieves information about packages, and rosdep installs system dependencies of a package.
The rqt plugin 'Introspection/Package Graph' visualizes package dependencies as a graph.
The roscd command, part of rosbash, performs a cd to the directory of a package, for example roscd roscpp_tutorials.
In Python, the RosPack class in the rospkg library provides package information, such as rospack.list() and rospack.get_path('rospy_tutorials').
In C++, ros::package in the roslib package provides information via ros::package::getPath('roslib') and ros::package::getAll(packages).
The page states that the ROS Wiki is for ROS 1, and ROS 2 users are directed to the ROS 2 Project Documentation at docs.ros.org.
